scope: 35 whole auxiliary records inspected as claims about scope/granularity, not as approvals of every entity on their listed pages. Exact source-first and current-record ledgers remain independently required.
source_basis: Frozen policy, approved chunk boundaries, source-scope-disposition.v3 with rendered maps, prior actual record/source-first passes and the explicitly re-read pages. Ownership is not semantic eligibility.

rows.review_disposition: Retire: 44–45 are eligible chapter-two source pages. A chunk-one context boundary is division of labour, not an exclusion from the whole-book benchmark.

Retain only bare citation markers, source-only apparatus and navigational cross-references as excluded regions. Page 7’s forward pointer does not exclude its substantive discussion of regional religion, Calas, commerce or institutions; attributed evidence remains eligible.

This is a granularity rule, not a blacklist of named places and people on entire pages. Retain under that narrow meaning, with no presumption that being an example makes useful subject access unnecessary.

Statistics are substantive supporting evidence for scale and comparison, not normally independent conceptual subjects. Retain numerical evidence wherever it carries the argument; none of the listed pages is excluded.

An anecdote need not become a separate unit, but it may contain a unique causal or interpretive distinction. Preserve that content under its relevant subject rather than requiring already developed terminology as a precondition.

Selective access is justified for regional comparison on 5–9. Preserve differences in environment, settlement, commerce, language, religion and jurisdiction; the rule excludes mechanical microheading multiplication, not meaningful place retrieval.

Replace density-only semantic permission with the frozen-policy exclusion of the page 3 map interior/key/credit. Literal caption remains eligible. This disposition is grounded in the separately rendered exact page and v3 scope decision.
Retire chunk-two context exclusion: 42–43 and 66–67 are eligible book pages assigned to adjacent owners; ownership does not remove source evidence from whole-book requirements.

Retain local nonmultiplication only. Publication, salon and institutional names can supply useful routes through developed reading/opinion subjects; attribution or brief mention alone neither compels nor forbids a separate requirement.

Retain numerical detail within the arguments about readership, affordability, institutional reach and finance. Remove a duration-based implication that support becomes eligible only when a policy is discussed at length.
The 62 pointer to 66–68 is navigation, not evidence proving unspecified later claims. Whole-book substantive Necker finance on those eligible pages remains in scope regardless of chapter ownership.

Retire duplicate erroneous map-policy boilerplate: chunk two has no identified map region in this record. The corrected global scope disposition and exact map-region records govern; no density permission survives.
Retire context-only record: 64–65 and 86–87 remain eligible through their owning source chunks.

Retain running heads, folios and production artifacts as excluded furniture. Distinguish repeated running chapter labels from substantive chapter/part headings, which remain eligible under the policy.

Bare markers are apparatus; names used only as attribution need not create biographies. The quotations themselves remain substantive evidence, and a witness’s developed treatment elsewhere remains eligible.

72/78/80/81 show concrete roles: first Estates-General taxing-right claim, inability to intervene abroad, exile of protesting magistrates and arrest of resistance leaders. Personal units are optional, but these actions and their consequences must survive in the relevant crisis subjects.

72 reports Mirabeau’s allegation of shady financial dealing during the pamphlet campaign. Exclude an asserted misconduct fact, but retain the allegation, its attribution and its contribution to public pressure on Calonne.

Individual dates/counts are not automatically separate subjects. Preserve essential sequence and vote/procedure distinctions, including uncertainty when dates conflict; usefulness does not require a narrowly scholarly audience.
Retire duplicate erroneous map-policy boilerplate; no identified map on these owned pages and no density-based semantic permission.

Retain only the rule against automatic promotion from a name mention. Lists can still contain independently useful people or institutional routes; no listed page or already reviewed subject is excluded.
Regional examples support economic, electoral and political variation. Preserve such contrasts and cross-chapter locality routes; sustained length is not a prerequisite for useful access.

Retain supporting employment, petitions, troops, voting and casualties as evidence for scale and action. Do not create standalone number headings or exclude quantitative qualifications from the parent arguments.

A speaker’s lack of sustained biography does not remove the political force of an epigram or ceremony. Retain quotations and vignettes as eligible event/idea evidence, with personal weighting optional.
Retire duplicate erroneous map-policy boilerplate without a map-page identity. Exact rendered-map scope governs elsewhere.
Retire chunk-five context exclusion: 110–111 and 136–137 remain eligible and cannot be described as without subject evidence in the integrated benchmark.
Retain repeated running heads and folios only. Substantive chapter text and captions, including mixed map pages, follow the separate source-region boundary.

Retain conditional nonmultiplication when no distinct access task is added; do not classify officeholders, locality examples or vote counts as inherently nonindexable. Recorded municipal, fiscal and constitutional distinctions remain.
Retain superscript markers/citation-only matter; absent endnotes cannot be reconstructed. Quoted or other substantive body text on these pages remains eligible.

113/115/126/130 provide municipal disturbance, rumour, administrative and fiscal examples. Separate microheadings are optional only while those differing mechanisms remain accessible under their parents.

Replace the density-only rule with semantic exclusion of map interiors and keys on 127 and 129. Their literal captions remain eligible; this does not erase prose on mixed pages or authorize geographic inferences from the graphics.
Retire ownership-only exclusion: 134–135 and 159–160 are eligible pages in the integrated scope.
Retain only nonautomatic personal weighting for brief exemplars/attributions. Political actors and witnesses with useful developed whole-book treatment retain their access.
Retain decree dates/votes as evidence within policy and event arguments. Do not remove temporal sequence, constitutional meaning or the separately tracked Gerle/Lafayette date conflicts.
144–145 give meaningful geography of the clerical oath. Preserve regional contrasts and explanatory variation within the oath/schism route; local microheadings need not each carry independent weight.

Retain rule against automatic biography from attribution; speakers’ words, letters and observations remain eligible substantive support. Note markers and unavailable endnote contents remain separate exclusions.
